    • 1. 1. Purpose and Scope
    • GHOST-MCP-ROOT
      1.1. GHOST MCP Capability Scope GHOST-MCP-ROOT GHOST shall provide a Model Context Protocol interface through which approved external AI clients can invoke explicitly exposed GHOST capabilities.

      The MCP capability shall provide a controlled external boundary around approved GHOST functions without transferring ownership of those functions to the MCP transport layer.

      MCP shall be represented as its own capability family in the GHOST requirement hierarchy.
      • GHOST-SRS-FILE-TREE
        2.8.1. Requirement File Tree Parent Anchor GHOST-SRS-FILE-TREE This requirement is the parent anchor for the approved StrictDoc child-file tree. Connected child dummy files shall reference this UID, or a child-file parent UID, through StrictDoc parent references so generated HTML can display navigable requirement relationships.
    GHOST-MCP-CAP-ROOT
    1.1. MCP Capability Scope GHOST-MCP-CAP-ROOT GHOST MCP shall support the approved Prompt Engineering capability and three non-ActiveBlackboard memory modes:

    - Episodic Memory;
    - Clipboard Memory; and
    - Collection Memory.

    ActiveBlackboard shall remain separately owned by 112_mcp_activeblackboard.sdoc.
    • GHOST-MCP-ENGINEER-PROMPT-TOOL
      2.1. GHOST Prompt Engineering Tool GHOST-MCP-ENGINEER-PROMPT-TOOL The MCP server shall expose the GHOST Prompt Engineering capability through the tool identifier:

      ghost_engineer_prompt

      The tool shall use the established GHOST prompt-processing path rather than implement an independent MCP-specific prompt-engineering algorithm.
      • GHOST-MCP-APPROVED-FLOW
        2.2. Prompt Engineering Processing Flow GHOST-MCP-APPROVED-FLOW The stable Prompt Engineering processing path shall:

        1. accept the current prompt text;
        2. create isolated request state;
        3. execute existing deterministic PreProcessing;
        4. execute existing A2 PromptShaper on the resulting SuperPrompt;
        5. rebuild the authoritative prompt-ready representation; and
        6. return the engineered prompt.

        Prompt Engineering shall not independently duplicate PreProcessing or A2 algorithms inside the MCP adapter.
        • GHOST-MCP-FRESH-SUPERPROMPT
          2.3. Fresh Prompt State Per Prompt-Engineering Call GHOST-MCP-FRESH-SUPERPROMPT Each Prompt Engineering call shall operate on request-isolated SuperPrompt state.

          Mutable prompt state from another user, request, or earlier tool call shall not be reused as the active processing state for the new call.
        • GHOST-MCP-PREPROCESS-CALL
          2.4. Existing PreProcessing Reuse GHOST-MCP-PREPROCESS-CALL The Prompt Engineering adapter shall invoke the existing GHOST deterministic PreProcessing behavior.

          It shall not implement a second MCP-specific parser, canonical-header model, default system, alias model, or prompt normalization algorithm.
          • GHOST-MCP-PREPROCESS-STAGE-GATE
            2.5. PreProcessing Completion Gate GHOST-MCP-PREPROCESS-STAGE-GATE A2 PromptShaper shall execute only after successful completion of the required PreProcessing operation for the same request.

            A failed PreProcessing operation shall not be represented as a successful engineered prompt.
            • GHOST-MCP-A2-CALL
              2.6. Existing A2 PromptShaper Reuse GHOST-MCP-A2-CALL The Prompt Engineering capability shall invoke the established A2 PromptShaper behavior and its existing Agent Stack infrastructure.

              The MCP adapter shall not create a second independent A2 prompt, selector implementation, field-write-back algorithm, or provider-specific A2 pipeline.
              • GHOST-MCP-A2-COMPLETION-GATE
                2.7. A2 Completion Gate GHOST-MCP-A2-COMPLETION-GATE A successful engineered-prompt result shall be produced only after the required A2 processing and final prompt projection have completed successfully.
                • GHOST-MCP-ENGINEERED-PROMPT-SOURCE
                  2.8. Authoritative Engineered Prompt Source GHOST-MCP-ENGINEERED-PROMPT-SOURCE The engineered prompt returned through MCP shall originate from the authoritative GHOST prompt-ready projection.

                  The MCP adapter shall not independently regenerate or paraphrase that engineered prompt.
      • GHOST-MCP-NO-ANSWER-GENERATION
        2.9. Prompt Engineering Is Not Answer Generation GHOST-MCP-NO-ANSWER-GENERATION The ghost_engineer_prompt operation itself shall remain a prompt-engineering capability.

        Its core GHOST operation shall not be redefined as the application's general final-answer generator.
      • GHOST-MCP-PROMPT-EXPERIMENT-BOUNDARY
        2.10. Experimental Prompt Modes Are Not Stable Requirements GHOST-MCP-PROMPT-EXPERIMENT-BOUNDARY Temporary implementation experiments that alter client behavior around ghost_engineer_prompt, including experimental Prompt:, MEM:, plain-request mode switching or supportive-context routing, shall not become stable product requirements unless separately approved.

        Their temporary presence in source code shall not require preservation in future MCP implementations.
    • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-MODEL
      3.1. Four-Mode MCP Memory Model GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-MODEL The approved GHOST MCP memory model shall consist of four conceptual memory modes:

      1. Episodic Memory.
      2. Clipboard Memory.
      3. Collection Memory.
      4. ActiveBlackboard Memory.

      This document owns the first three modes.

      ActiveBlackboard is owned exclusively by 112_mcp_activeblackboard.sdoc.
      • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-COMMON-TRUTH
        3.2. Common Durable Memory Infrastructure GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-COMMON-TRUTH MCP memory modes may reuse the established GHOST durable-memory infrastructure, including:

        - MemoryRecord;
        - .ragmem durable episode bodies;
        - .ragmeta.json metadata;
        - SQLite indexing; and
        - vector storage where required by the owning memory mode.

        MCP-specific semantics shall not require creation of a second unrelated memory truth model when the common GHOST infrastructure can represent the approved behavior.
        • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-OWNER-SCOPE
          3.3. Owner-Scoped Memory GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-OWNER-SCOPE Every persistent MCP memory operation shall be scoped to the authenticated owner.

          An exact key, record ID, Collection ID, Collection Name, Clipboard slot, or other selector shall never bypass owner isolation.
      • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE
        4.1.1. Shared Save Concept GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE GHOST shall expose one clear Save concept for ordinary memory episodes.

        The current executable tool identifier ghost_memory_tag represents the existing implementation of this save concept.

        A future rename of that tool is not approved by this requirement and shall require a separate interface-contract decision.
        • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-VISIBLE-CONTENT
          4.1.2. Save Visible Conversation Content GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-VISIBLE-CONTENT When saving a visible conversation episode, the selected visible user content and corresponding visible assistant content shall be stored without substitution by hidden reasoning, internal tool traffic, or an internal model/tool result.

          When exact visible content is required by the selected Save operation, ChatGPT shall pass that content without summarizing it.
        • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-TITLE-DESCRIPTION
          4.1.3. Episode Title and Description GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-TITLE-DESCRIPTION A newly saved ordinary memory episode shall have:

          - an Episode Title; and
          - an Episode Description.

          ChatGPT shall generate both from the selected visible episode unless a more specific mode requirement states otherwise.

          Episode Title is primarily human-facing metadata.

          Episode Description is the compact semantic description used by intelligent Episodic retrieval.
        • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-RECALL-KEY
          4.1.4. Recall Key Handling and Episodic Uniqueness GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-RECALL-KEY When the user explicitly provides a Recall Key, ChatGPT shall pass that key.

          When the user requests an Episodic save without providing a Recall Key, ChatGPT shall generate an appropriate Recall Key rather than forcing the user to invent one.

          Within an authenticated owner's Episodic Memory, the effective Recall Key shall be unique.

          Before saving a new Episodic episode, GHOST shall check the owner-scoped Episodic Recall Keys recorded in the SQLite/index layer.

          If the requested or generated base key is already used by an Episodic episode, GHOST shall deterministically allocate the next available numeric suffix using the form:

          base_key_1
          base_key_2
          base_key_3

          and so on.

          The originally supplied key shall remain the base key; GHOST shall not overwrite the existing episode.

          The successful save result shall return the actual effective Recall Key that was stored.
      • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-RECALL
        4.2.1. Shared Recall Concept GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-RECALL GHOST shall expose one Recall concept capable of selecting the appropriate retrieval path from the user's request.

        For Episodic Memory, Recall shall support:

        - deterministic exact retrieval when an exact Recall Key or exact Record ID is known; and
        - intelligent semantic retrieval when the user describes a memory without knowing its exact identifier.

        The two paths access the same Episodic Memory domain.
        • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-EXACT-RECALL
          4.2.2. Exact Recall GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-EXACT-RECALL An exact Recall Key or exact Record ID shall be handled deterministically.

          Exact identifiers shall directly select stored records within the authenticated owner's scope.

          Exact Recall shall not require semantic vector ranking.
        • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-NO-FAKE-EXACT-FILTER
          4.2.3. Exact Identifiers Are Not Intelligent-Retrieval Filters GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-NO-FAKE-EXACT-FILTER Recall Key and Record ID shall not be treated as approximate SQL narrowing filters for intelligent semantic retrieval.

          When an exact identifier is supplied, GHOST shall use the deterministic exact path.

          When the identifier is unknown, GHOST shall use the intelligent Episodic retrieval path defined in this document.
      • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-LIST
        4.3.1. Shared Memory List GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-LIST ghost_memory_list shall provide metadata discovery and navigation rather than full episode retrieval.

        The shared list capability shall be available for memory modes where listing is meaningful, except Clipboard Memory.

        The list capability may return identifying and descriptive metadata such as:

        - memory or conversation name;
        - memory type;
        - Recall Key;
        - Record ID;
        - Episode Title;
        - Episode Description; and
        - creation time.

        Stored full input/output bodies shall remain Recall content rather than List content.
        • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-LIST-FILTERS
          4.3.2. Deterministic List Filters GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-LIST-FILTERS The shared memory list operation shall support deterministic metadata filtering sufficient for practical discovery.

          Approved filter dimensions include:

          - memory or conversation name;
          - memory type;
          - date range; and
          - deterministic description matching.

          List shall not silently become semantic full-memory retrieval.
      • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE
        4.4.1. Deterministic Memory Delete GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE ghost_memory_delete shall delete individual memory episodes only through an exact selector:

        - exact Recall Key; or
        - exact Record ID.

        Delete shall never use semantic similarity, a natural-language description, Episode Description similarity, vector retrieval, fuzzy matching, or an LLM decision to choose what data to destroy.
        • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-DUPLICATE-SAFETY
          4.4.2. Duplicate Recall-Key Safety GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-DUPLICATE-SAFETY If an exact Recall Key resolves to multiple owner-scoped records, GHOST shall not silently choose an arbitrary record for deletion.

          The user shall be given deterministic identifiers sufficient to select the intended episode, or shall explicitly request deletion of all exact matches where that behavior is supported.
        • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-NO-CLIPBOARD
          4.4.3. Clipboard Excluded from Generic Delete GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-NO-CLIPBOARD Clipboard Memory shall not participate in the generic ghost_memory_delete operation.

          Clipboard lifecycle shall be controlled by its dedicated short-retention policy.
      • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-ROOT
        5.1. Episodic Memory Scope GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-ROOT Episodic Memory shall store ordinary persistent memory episodes that can later be recovered either:

        - directly through an exact Recall Key or Record ID; or
        - intelligently from a natural-language description.

        Direct Recall and intelligent retrieval shall be two access paths to the same Episodic Memory rather than separate memory types.
        • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DESCRIPTION-REQUIRED
          5.2. Episode Description Required for Episodic Save GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DESCRIPTION-REQUIRED Each newly saved Episodic Memory episode shall contain a non-empty Episode Description.

          The description shall summarize the semantic content or useful meaning of that individual episode sufficiently to support later intelligent retrieval.

          The Episode Description shall not be replaced by the Episode Title.
          • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DESCRIPTION-VECTOR
            5.3. Episode Description Embedding GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DESCRIPTION-VECTOR The Episode Description shall have a precomputed vector representation available for intelligent Episodic retrieval.

            The description embedding shall be created from the stored Episode Description rather than generated dynamically from the complete episode during every recall.
        • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-INTELLIGENT-QUERY
          5.4. Intelligent Recall Query Description GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-INTELLIGENT-QUERY When the user requests a memory without knowing an exact identifier, ChatGPT shall formulate the semantic description of the memory being sought.

          That query description shall be embedded at recall time and compared against stored Episode Description embeddings.
          • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DATE-NARROWING
            5.5. Optional Date Narrowing GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DATE-NARROWING Intelligent Episodic retrieval may first apply a deterministic SQL date-range filter when the user's request provides a relevant date or date interval.

            Date range is the approved deterministic narrowing dimension for the intelligent Episodic retrieval path.

            The intelligent path shall not invent key-prefix, title-prefix, or approximate Recall Key filtering as additional narrowing mechanisms.
          • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-COSINE-RANKING
            5.6. Episode Description Similarity Ranking GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-COSINE-RANKING After any optional date narrowing, intelligent Episodic retrieval shall compare the query-description vector with stored Episode Description vectors using cosine similarity or the equivalent cosine-ranking behavior of the selected vector implementation.

            Ranking shall be based primarily on Episode Description semantics.
            • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CANDIDATE-RETURN
              5.7. Compact Intelligent Recall Candidates GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CANDIDATE-RETURN The intelligent retrieval stage shall return only a small ranked candidate set to the client model.

              The target candidate set shall normally contain approximately five to ten candidates.

              Each candidate shall provide sufficient metadata for selection, including at least:

              - Record ID; and
              - Episode Description.

              The candidate stage shall not return the complete stored Q/A bodies for every candidate.
              • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CLIENT-SELECTION
                5.8. Client Model Candidate Selection GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CLIENT-SELECTION After receiving the compact ranked candidate descriptions, the invoking AI client may use the user's request and candidate descriptions to select the intended episode.

                The selection result shall resolve to an exact Record ID before the full episode is fetched.
                • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-EXACT-FINAL-FETCH
                  5.9. Exact Final Episode Fetch GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-EXACT-FINAL-FETCH After intelligent candidate selection, GHOST shall fetch the chosen full episode deterministically by exact Record ID.

                  Full episode content shall be loaded only after the candidate-selection step has resolved the exact stored record.
            • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-NO-TITLE-FIRST-FUNNEL
              5.10. No Mandatory Title-First Semantic Funnel GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-NO-TITLE-FIRST-FUNNEL Episode Title shall remain useful human-facing metadata but shall not be a mandatory first semantic-ranking stage before Episode Description similarity.

              The approved intelligent-retrieval path shall rank Episode Descriptions directly.
      • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-ROOT
        6.1. Clipboard Memory Scope GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-ROOT Clipboard Memory shall provide short-lived, deterministic temporary memory slots for lightweight save-and-recall workflows.

        Clipboard Memory shall use the reserved slot identifiers:

        M1 through M100.
        • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RESERVED-KEYS
          6.2. Reserved Clipboard Routing GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RESERVED-KEYS M1 through M100 shall be reserved for Clipboard Memory.

          A normal Episodic save shall not silently store an M1-M100 key as an ordinary Episodic Recall Key.

          When a user explicitly requests saving to or recalling from M1-M100, the request shall be routed to Clipboard Memory behavior.
        • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-DAILY-FILE
          6.3. One Clipboard File Per Day GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-DAILY-FILE For each authenticated owner, Clipboard Memory shall use at most one Clipboard memory history file for a UTC day in which Clipboard content is saved.

          Clipboard storage shall not perform intra-day file rollover merely because several Clipboard episodes are appended.
        • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-APPEND-ONLY
          6.4. Append-Only Clipboard Storage GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-APPEND-ONLY Clipboard writes shall be append-only.

          Saving to an already used slot shall append a new episode with the same slot identifier rather than physically overwriting the older episode.

          For example, repeated saves to M7 may produce several historical M7 episodes in durable storage.
          • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-LATEST-RECALL
            6.5. Newest Matching Clipboard Recall GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-LATEST-RECALL Recall of a Clipboard slot shall return the newest owner-scoped episode with that exact slot identifier.

            Creation timestamps and deterministic ordering metadata shall be sufficient to identify the newest matching episode.
        • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-CONTENT
          6.6. Clipboard Episode Content GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-CONTENT A Clipboard episode shall store only the visible saved content and metadata required for deterministic slot storage and recall.

          Clipboard episodes shall not require or generate an Episode Description.

          Clipboard episodes shall not maintain an ActiveBrief.
        • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-NO-SEMANTIC-RETRIEVAL
          6.7. Clipboard Uses Exact Slot Recall Only GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-NO-SEMANTIC-RETRIEVAL Clipboard Memory shall not provide intelligent semantic retrieval.

          Clipboard Recall shall use the exact M1-M100 slot identifier and return the newest exact match.
        • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-NO-GENERIC-LIST-DELETE
          6.8. Clipboard Outside Generic List and Delete GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-NO-GENERIC-LIST-DELETE Clipboard Memory shall not participate in the shared generic memory List or Delete operations.

          The user-facing model shall treat Clipboard as a temporary slot mechanism rather than as a manually administered long-term memory archive.
        • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RETENTION
          6.9. Short Clipboard Retention GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RETENTION Clipboard Memory shall be short-lived.

          The approved default retention window shall be approximately ten days, represented through explicit expiration metadata rather than inferred from a filename.

          Expired Clipboard histories shall be eligible for physical deletion together with their corresponding SQLite index rows.
          • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-STARTUP-CLEANUP
            6.10. Asynchronous Expired Clipboard Cleanup GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-STARTUP-CLEANUP Expired Clipboard memory cleanup shall run asynchronously during MCP/server startup.

            Startup cleanup shall use authoritative expiration metadata and shall remove expired durable Clipboard files and corresponding index records coherently.
      • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ROOT
        7.1. Collection Memory Scope GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ROOT Collection Memory shall provide a persistent topic-oriented container into which explicitly requested memory episodes can be appended over time.

        A Collection is not an automatically recorded conversation.

        A Collection groups intentionally saved episodes around a user-defined subject or purpose.
        • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INIT
          7.2. Collection Initialization GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INIT Creating a Collection shall require:

          - Collection Name; and
          - Collection Description or Purpose.

          Initialization shall create a stable Collection identity and shall record its creation time.

          The underlying stable file_id shall serve as the Collection ID.
          • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-IDENTITY
            7.3. Stable Collection Identity GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-IDENTITY Collection ID shall remain stable independently of later episode appends.

            A Collection may be targeted for an append by:

            - exact Collection ID; or
            - exact Collection Name where that name resolves safely within the authenticated owner's scope.
        • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-EXPLICIT-APPEND
          7.4. Collection Append Is Explicit GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-EXPLICIT-APPEND A Collection shall receive a new episode only when the user explicitly asks GHOST to save or add content to that Collection.

          Normal conversation turns shall not be appended automatically merely because a Collection exists.
          • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-EPISODE-METADATA
            7.5. Collection Episode Description GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-EPISODE-METADATA Every appended Collection episode shall contain an Episode Description describing that episode's local contribution to the Collection.

            A Recall Key may be explicitly supplied or generated according to the shared Save policy.
          • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ACTIVEBRIEF
            7.6. Collection Cumulative ActiveBrief GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ACTIVEBRIEF Every appended Collection episode shall also carry the current cumulative Collection ActiveBrief.

            The Collection ActiveBrief shall summarize the accumulated knowledge or state of the Collection's fixed topic after incorporating the new episode.

            The Collection ActiveBrief is not a conversation-summary mechanism and shall not be confused with ActiveBlackboard merely because both use an ActiveBrief concept.
        • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-LIST
          7.7. List Collections GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-LIST GHOST shall support listing Collections for the authenticated owner.

          The Collection list shall provide sufficient metadata for deterministic identification, including at least:

          - Collection ID;
          - Collection Name;
          - Collection Description or Purpose; and
          - creation date.
          • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-LIST-EPISODES
            7.8. List Episodes in a Collection GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-LIST-EPISODES Given an exact Collection ID, GHOST shall support listing the episodes belonging to that Collection.

            The episode list shall return metadata for all Collection episodes, including:

            - Recall Key where present; and
            - Episode Description.

            This operation is metadata navigation and shall not automatically return the complete stored content of every episode.
        • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INDIVIDUAL-RECALL
          7.9. Individual Collection Episode Recall GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INDIVIDUAL-RECALL An individual Collection episode shall not require a separate Collection-specific recall mechanism when it has an exact Recall Key or Record ID.

          The shared exact Recall capability shall be used for an individual episode.
        • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-RECALL
          7.10. Collection Episode Range Recall GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-RECALL GHOST shall support Collection-specific retrieval by episode number or episode range.

          Examples include:

          - one episode such as episode 3; or
          - a range such as episodes 2 through 7.

          Episode ordering shall be deterministic within the Collection.
          • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-TOKEN-SAFETY
            7.11. Token-Safe Collection Range Recall GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-TOKEN-SAFETY When a requested Collection range would produce more content than can be returned safely in the active client/model context, GHOST may return a deterministic prefix of the requested range.

            The response shall explicitly identify the unreturned remainder so that the client can request it subsequently.

            The exact token threshold or page size is intentionally not fixed by this requirement.
        • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-WHOLE
          7.12. Whole Collection Delete GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-WHOLE Deleting an entire Collection shall be a separate destructive operation from deleting an individual memory episode.

          Whole-Collection deletion shall require the exact Collection ID.

          A Collection shall not be destroyed by semantic description, Collection Name similarity, or LLM selection.
          • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-CONFIRMATION
            7.13. Two-Step Whole Collection Delete Safety GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-CONFIRMATION Whole-Collection deletion shall use a temporary server-side confirmation state.

            For an authenticated owner and exact Collection ID, the first exact whole-Collection delete request shall not execute the deletion.

            The first request shall set the corresponding server-side delete-pending state to true and shall return a warning or refusal asking the client/user to repeat the same exact Collection deletion request.

            If the same owner repeats the exact whole-Collection delete request for the same Collection ID while that delete-pending state is true, GHOST shall execute the deletion and confirm the result.

            The delete-pending state shall be volatile server state and shall reset to false when the MCP server restarts.

            A future timeout or asynchronous reset policy may be added later, but no timeout duration or additional reset mechanism is fixed by this requirement.
        • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INDIVIDUAL-DELETE
          7.14. Individual Collection Episode Delete GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INDIVIDUAL-DELETE Deleting an individual episode from a Collection shall use the shared deterministic memory Delete behavior.

          No separate Collection-specific single-episode deletion contract is required.
    • GHOST-MCP-CAP-NO-IMPLEMENTATION-INVENTION
      8.1. No False Implementation Claim GHOST-MCP-CAP-NO-IMPLEMENTATION-INVENTION A requirement in this document shall not be reported as currently implemented solely because underlying data fields or partial infrastructure already exist.

      Implementation status shall require corresponding executable behavior and verification.

    2. 2. Prompt Engineering
    • GHOST-MCP-CAP-ROOT
      1.1. MCP Capability Scope GHOST-MCP-CAP-ROOT GHOST MCP shall support the approved Prompt Engineering capability and three non-ActiveBlackboard memory modes:

      - Episodic Memory;
      - Clipboard Memory; and
      - Collection Memory.

      ActiveBlackboard shall remain separately owned by 112_mcp_activeblackboard.sdoc.
      • GHOST-MCP-ROOT
        1.1. GHOST MCP Capability Scope GHOST-MCP-ROOT GHOST shall provide a Model Context Protocol interface through which approved external AI clients can invoke explicitly exposed GHOST capabilities.

        The MCP capability shall provide a controlled external boundary around approved GHOST functions without transferring ownership of those functions to the MCP transport layer.

        MCP shall be represented as its own capability family in the GHOST requirement hierarchy.

          2.8.1. Requirement File Tree Parent Anchor GHOST-SRS-FILE-TREE This requirement is the parent anchor for the approved StrictDoc child-file tree. Connected child dummy files shall reference this UID, or a child-file parent UID, through StrictDoc parent references so generated HTML can display navigable requirement relationships.
    GHOST-MCP-ENGINEER-PROMPT-TOOL
    2.1. GHOST Prompt Engineering Tool GHOST-MCP-ENGINEER-PROMPT-TOOL The MCP server shall expose the GHOST Prompt Engineering capability through the tool identifier:

    ghost_engineer_prompt

    The tool shall use the established GHOST prompt-processing path rather than implement an independent MCP-specific prompt-engineering algorithm.
    • GHOST-MCP-APPROVED-FLOW
      2.2. Prompt Engineering Processing Flow GHOST-MCP-APPROVED-FLOW The stable Prompt Engineering processing path shall:

      1. accept the current prompt text;
      2. create isolated request state;
      3. execute existing deterministic PreProcessing;
      4. execute existing A2 PromptShaper on the resulting SuperPrompt;
      5. rebuild the authoritative prompt-ready representation; and
      6. return the engineered prompt.

      Prompt Engineering shall not independently duplicate PreProcessing or A2 algorithms inside the MCP adapter.
      • GHOST-MCP-FRESH-SUPERPROMPT
        2.3. Fresh Prompt State Per Prompt-Engineering Call GHOST-MCP-FRESH-SUPERPROMPT Each Prompt Engineering call shall operate on request-isolated SuperPrompt state.

        Mutable prompt state from another user, request, or earlier tool call shall not be reused as the active processing state for the new call.
      • GHOST-MCP-PREPROCESS-CALL
        2.4. Existing PreProcessing Reuse GHOST-MCP-PREPROCESS-CALL The Prompt Engineering adapter shall invoke the existing GHOST deterministic PreProcessing behavior.

        It shall not implement a second MCP-specific parser, canonical-header model, default system, alias model, or prompt normalization algorithm.
        • GHOST-MCP-PREPROCESS-STAGE-GATE
          2.5. PreProcessing Completion Gate GHOST-MCP-PREPROCESS-STAGE-GATE A2 PromptShaper shall execute only after successful completion of the required PreProcessing operation for the same request.

          A failed PreProcessing operation shall not be represented as a successful engineered prompt.
          • GHOST-MCP-A2-CALL
            2.6. Existing A2 PromptShaper Reuse GHOST-MCP-A2-CALL The Prompt Engineering capability shall invoke the established A2 PromptShaper behavior and its existing Agent Stack infrastructure.

            The MCP adapter shall not create a second independent A2 prompt, selector implementation, field-write-back algorithm, or provider-specific A2 pipeline.
            • GHOST-MCP-A2-COMPLETION-GATE
              2.7. A2 Completion Gate GHOST-MCP-A2-COMPLETION-GATE A successful engineered-prompt result shall be produced only after the required A2 processing and final prompt projection have completed successfully.
              • GHOST-MCP-ENGINEERED-PROMPT-SOURCE
                2.8. Authoritative Engineered Prompt Source GHOST-MCP-ENGINEERED-PROMPT-SOURCE The engineered prompt returned through MCP shall originate from the authoritative GHOST prompt-ready projection.

                The MCP adapter shall not independently regenerate or paraphrase that engineered prompt.
    • GHOST-MCP-NO-ANSWER-GENERATION
      2.9. Prompt Engineering Is Not Answer Generation GHOST-MCP-NO-ANSWER-GENERATION The ghost_engineer_prompt operation itself shall remain a prompt-engineering capability.

      Its core GHOST operation shall not be redefined as the application's general final-answer generator.
    • GHOST-MCP-PROMPT-EXPERIMENT-BOUNDARY
      2.10. Experimental Prompt Modes Are Not Stable Requirements GHOST-MCP-PROMPT-EXPERIMENT-BOUNDARY Temporary implementation experiments that alter client behavior around ghost_engineer_prompt, including experimental Prompt:, MEM:, plain-request mode switching or supportive-context routing, shall not become stable product requirements unless separately approved.

      Their temporary presence in source code shall not require preservation in future MCP implementations.

    2.8. Authoritative Engineered Prompt Source GHOST-MCP-ENGINEERED-PROMPT-SOURCE The engineered prompt returned through MCP shall originate from the authoritative GHOST prompt-ready projection.

    The MCP adapter shall not independently regenerate or paraphrase that engineered prompt.
    • GHOST-MCP-ENGINEER-PROMPT-TOOL
      2.1. GHOST Prompt Engineering Tool GHOST-MCP-ENGINEER-PROMPT-TOOL The MCP server shall expose the GHOST Prompt Engineering capability through the tool identifier:

      ghost_engineer_prompt

      The tool shall use the established GHOST prompt-processing path rather than implement an independent MCP-specific prompt-engineering algorithm.
      • GHOST-MCP-CAP-ROOT
        1.1. MCP Capability Scope GHOST-MCP-CAP-ROOT GHOST MCP shall support the approved Prompt Engineering capability and three non-ActiveBlackboard memory modes:

        - Episodic Memory;
        - Clipboard Memory; and
        - Collection Memory.

        ActiveBlackboard shall remain separately owned by 112_mcp_activeblackboard.sdoc.

          The MCP capability shall provide a controlled external boundary around approved GHOST functions without transferring ownership of those functions to the MCP transport layer.

          MCP shall be represented as its own capability family in the GHOST requirement hierarchy.

    3. 3. MCP Memory Model
    • GHOST-MCP-CAP-ROOT
      1.1. MCP Capability Scope GHOST-MCP-CAP-ROOT GHOST MCP shall support the approved Prompt Engineering capability and three non-ActiveBlackboard memory modes:

      - Episodic Memory;
      - Clipboard Memory; and

        The MCP capability shall provide a controlled external boundary around approved GHOST functions without transferring ownership of those functions to the MCP transport layer.

        MCP shall be represented as its own capability family in the GHOST requirement hierarchy.

Connected child dummy files shall reference this UID, or a child-file parent UID, through StrictDoc parent references so generated HTML can display navigable requirement relationships.
    GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-MODEL
    3.1. Four-Mode MCP Memory Model GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-MODEL The approved GHOST MCP memory model shall consist of four conceptual memory modes:

    1. Episodic Memory.
    2. Clipboard Memory.
    3. Collection Memory.
    4. ActiveBlackboard Memory.

    This document owns the first three modes.

    ActiveBlackboard is owned exclusively by 112_mcp_activeblackboard.sdoc.
    • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-COMMON-TRUTH
      3.2. Common Durable Memory Infrastructure GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-COMMON-TRUTH MCP memory modes may reuse the established GHOST durable-memory infrastructure, including:

      - MemoryRecord;
      - .ragmem durable episode bodies;
      - .ragmeta.json metadata;
      - SQLite indexing; and
      - vector storage where required by the owning memory mode.

      MCP-specific semantics shall not require creation of a second unrelated memory truth model when the common GHOST infrastructure can represent the approved behavior.
      • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-OWNER-SCOPE
        3.3. Owner-Scoped Memory GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-OWNER-SCOPE Every persistent MCP memory operation shall be scoped to the authenticated owner.

        An exact key, record ID, Collection ID, Collection Name, Clipboard slot, or other selector shall never bypass owner isolation.
    • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE
      4.1.1. Shared Save Concept GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE GHOST shall expose one clear Save concept for ordinary memory episodes.

      The current executable tool identifier ghost_memory_tag represents the existing implementation of this save concept.

      A future rename of that tool is not approved by this requirement and shall require a separate interface-contract decision.
      • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-VISIBLE-CONTENT
        4.1.2. Save Visible Conversation Content GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-VISIBLE-CONTENT When saving a visible conversation episode, the selected visible user content and corresponding visible assistant content shall be stored without substitution by hidden reasoning, internal tool traffic, or an internal model/tool result.

        When exact visible content is required by the selected Save operation, ChatGPT shall pass that content without summarizing it.
      • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-TITLE-DESCRIPTION
        4.1.3. Episode Title and Description GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-TITLE-DESCRIPTION A newly saved ordinary memory episode shall have:

        - an Episode Title; and
        - an Episode Description.

        ChatGPT shall generate both from the selected visible episode unless a more specific mode requirement states otherwise.

        Episode Title is primarily human-facing metadata.

        Episode Description is the compact semantic description used by intelligent Episodic retrieval.
      • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-RECALL-KEY
        4.1.4. Recall Key Handling and Episodic Uniqueness GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-RECALL-KEY When the user explicitly provides a Recall Key, ChatGPT shall pass that key.

        When the user requests an Episodic save without providing a Recall Key, ChatGPT shall generate an appropriate Recall Key rather than forcing the user to invent one.

        Within an authenticated owner's Episodic Memory, the effective Recall Key shall be unique.

        Before saving a new Episodic episode, GHOST shall check the owner-scoped Episodic Recall Keys recorded in the SQLite/index layer.

        If the requested or generated base key is already used by an Episodic episode, GHOST shall deterministically allocate the next available numeric suffix using the form:

        base_key_1
        base_key_2
        base_key_3

        and so on.

        The originally supplied key shall remain the base key; GHOST shall not overwrite the existing episode.

        The successful save result shall return the actual effective Recall Key that was stored.
    • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-RECALL
      4.2.1. Shared Recall Concept GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-RECALL GHOST shall expose one Recall concept capable of selecting the appropriate retrieval path from the user's request.

      For Episodic Memory, Recall shall support:

      - deterministic exact retrieval when an exact Recall Key or exact Record ID is known; and
      - intelligent semantic retrieval when the user describes a memory without knowing its exact identifier.

      The two paths access the same Episodic Memory domain.
      • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-EXACT-RECALL
        4.2.2. Exact Recall GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-EXACT-RECALL An exact Recall Key or exact Record ID shall be handled deterministically.

        Exact identifiers shall directly select stored records within the authenticated owner's scope.

        Exact Recall shall not require semantic vector ranking.
      • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-NO-FAKE-EXACT-FILTER
        4.2.3. Exact Identifiers Are Not Intelligent-Retrieval Filters GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-NO-FAKE-EXACT-FILTER Recall Key and Record ID shall not be treated as approximate SQL narrowing filters for intelligent semantic retrieval.

        When an exact identifier is supplied, GHOST shall use the deterministic exact path.

        When the identifier is unknown, GHOST shall use the intelligent Episodic retrieval path defined in this document.
    • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-LIST
      4.3.1. Shared Memory List GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-LIST ghost_memory_list shall provide metadata discovery and navigation rather than full episode retrieval.

      The shared list capability shall be available for memory modes where listing is meaningful, except Clipboard Memory.

      The list capability may return identifying and descriptive metadata such as:

      - memory or conversation name;
      - memory type;
      - Recall Key;
      - Record ID;
      - Episode Title;
      - Episode Description; and
      - creation time.

      Stored full input/output bodies shall remain Recall content rather than List content.
      • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-LIST-FILTERS
        4.3.2. Deterministic List Filters GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-LIST-FILTERS The shared memory list operation shall support deterministic metadata filtering sufficient for practical discovery.

        Approved filter dimensions include:

        - memory or conversation name;
        - memory type;
        - date range; and
        - deterministic description matching.

        List shall not silently become semantic full-memory retrieval.
    • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE
      4.4.1. Deterministic Memory Delete GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE ghost_memory_delete shall delete individual memory episodes only through an exact selector:

      - exact Recall Key; or
      - exact Record ID.

      Delete shall never use semantic similarity, a natural-language description, Episode Description similarity, vector retrieval, fuzzy matching, or an LLM decision to choose what data to destroy.
      • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-DUPLICATE-SAFETY
        4.4.2. Duplicate Recall-Key Safety GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-DUPLICATE-SAFETY If an exact Recall Key resolves to multiple owner-scoped records, GHOST shall not silently choose an arbitrary record for deletion.

        The user shall be given deterministic identifiers sufficient to select the intended episode, or shall explicitly request deletion of all exact matches where that behavior is supported.
      • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-NO-CLIPBOARD
        4.4.3. Clipboard Excluded from Generic Delete GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-NO-CLIPBOARD Clipboard Memory shall not participate in the generic ghost_memory_delete operation.

        Clipboard lifecycle shall be controlled by its dedicated short-retention policy.
    • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-ROOT
      5.1. Episodic Memory Scope GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-ROOT Episodic Memory shall store ordinary persistent memory episodes that can later be recovered either:

      - directly through an exact Recall Key or Record ID; or
      - intelligently from a natural-language description.

      Direct Recall and intelligent retrieval shall be two access paths to the same Episodic Memory rather than separate memory types.
      • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DESCRIPTION-REQUIRED
        5.2. Episode Description Required for Episodic Save GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DESCRIPTION-REQUIRED Each newly saved Episodic Memory episode shall contain a non-empty Episode Description.

        The description shall summarize the semantic content or useful meaning of that individual episode sufficiently to support later intelligent retrieval.

        The Episode Description shall not be replaced by the Episode Title.
        • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DESCRIPTION-VECTOR
          5.3. Episode Description Embedding GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DESCRIPTION-VECTOR The Episode Description shall have a precomputed vector representation available for intelligent Episodic retrieval.

          The description embedding shall be created from the stored Episode Description rather than generated dynamically from the complete episode during every recall.
      • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-INTELLIGENT-QUERY
        5.4. Intelligent Recall Query Description GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-INTELLIGENT-QUERY When the user requests a memory without knowing an exact identifier, ChatGPT shall formulate the semantic description of the memory being sought.

        That query description shall be embedded at recall time and compared against stored Episode Description embeddings.
        • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DATE-NARROWING
          5.5. Optional Date Narrowing GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DATE-NARROWING Intelligent Episodic retrieval may first apply a deterministic SQL date-range filter when the user's request provides a relevant date or date interval.

          Date range is the approved deterministic narrowing dimension for the intelligent Episodic retrieval path.

          The intelligent path shall not invent key-prefix, title-prefix, or approximate Recall Key filtering as additional narrowing mechanisms.
        • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-COSINE-RANKING
          5.6. Episode Description Similarity Ranking GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-COSINE-RANKING After any optional date narrowing, intelligent Episodic retrieval shall compare the query-description vector with stored Episode Description vectors using cosine similarity or the equivalent cosine-ranking behavior of the selected vector implementation.

          Ranking shall be based primarily on Episode Description semantics.
          • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CANDIDATE-RETURN
            5.7. Compact Intelligent Recall Candidates GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CANDIDATE-RETURN The intelligent retrieval stage shall return only a small ranked candidate set to the client model.

            The target candidate set shall normally contain approximately five to ten candidates.

            Each candidate shall provide sufficient metadata for selection, including at least:

            - Record ID; and
            - Episode Description.

            The candidate stage shall not return the complete stored Q/A bodies for every candidate.
            • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CLIENT-SELECTION
              5.8. Client Model Candidate Selection GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CLIENT-SELECTION After receiving the compact ranked candidate descriptions, the invoking AI client may use the user's request and candidate descriptions to select the intended episode.

              The selection result shall resolve to an exact Record ID before the full episode is fetched.
              • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-EXACT-FINAL-FETCH
                5.9. Exact Final Episode Fetch GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-EXACT-FINAL-FETCH After intelligent candidate selection, GHOST shall fetch the chosen full episode deterministically by exact Record ID.

                Full episode content shall be loaded only after the candidate-selection step has resolved the exact stored record.
          • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-NO-TITLE-FIRST-FUNNEL
            5.10. No Mandatory Title-First Semantic Funnel GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-NO-TITLE-FIRST-FUNNEL Episode Title shall remain useful human-facing metadata but shall not be a mandatory first semantic-ranking stage before Episode Description similarity.

            The approved intelligent-retrieval path shall rank Episode Descriptions directly.
    • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-ROOT
      6.1. Clipboard Memory Scope GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-ROOT Clipboard Memory shall provide short-lived, deterministic temporary memory slots for lightweight save-and-recall workflows.

      Clipboard Memory shall use the reserved slot identifiers:

      M1 through M100.
      • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RESERVED-KEYS
        6.2. Reserved Clipboard Routing GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RESERVED-KEYS M1 through M100 shall be reserved for Clipboard Memory.

        A normal Episodic save shall not silently store an M1-M100 key as an ordinary Episodic Recall Key.

        When a user explicitly requests saving to or recalling from M1-M100, the request shall be routed to Clipboard Memory behavior.
      • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-DAILY-FILE
        6.3. One Clipboard File Per Day GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-DAILY-FILE For each authenticated owner, Clipboard Memory shall use at most one Clipboard memory history file for a UTC day in which Clipboard content is saved.

        Clipboard storage shall not perform intra-day file rollover merely because several Clipboard episodes are appended.
      • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-APPEND-ONLY
        6.4. Append-Only Clipboard Storage GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-APPEND-ONLY Clipboard writes shall be append-only.

        Saving to an already used slot shall append a new episode with the same slot identifier rather than physically overwriting the older episode.

        For example, repeated saves to M7 may produce several historical M7 episodes in durable storage.
        • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-LATEST-RECALL
          6.5. Newest Matching Clipboard Recall GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-LATEST-RECALL Recall of a Clipboard slot shall return the newest owner-scoped episode with that exact slot identifier.

          Creation timestamps and deterministic ordering metadata shall be sufficient to identify the newest matching episode.
      • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-CONTENT
        6.6. Clipboard Episode Content GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-CONTENT A Clipboard episode shall store only the visible saved content and metadata required for deterministic slot storage and recall.

        Clipboard episodes shall not require or generate an Episode Description.

        Clipboard episodes shall not maintain an ActiveBrief.
      • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-NO-SEMANTIC-RETRIEVAL
        6.7. Clipboard Uses Exact Slot Recall Only GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-NO-SEMANTIC-RETRIEVAL Clipboard Memory shall not provide intelligent semantic retrieval.

        Clipboard Recall shall use the exact M1-M100 slot identifier and return the newest exact match.
      • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-NO-GENERIC-LIST-DELETE
        6.8. Clipboard Outside Generic List and Delete GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-NO-GENERIC-LIST-DELETE Clipboard Memory shall not participate in the shared generic memory List or Delete operations.

        The user-facing model shall treat Clipboard as a temporary slot mechanism rather than as a manually administered long-term memory archive.
      • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RETENTION
        6.9. Short Clipboard Retention GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RETENTION Clipboard Memory shall be short-lived.

        The approved default retention window shall be approximately ten days, represented through explicit expiration metadata rather than inferred from a filename.

        Expired Clipboard histories shall be eligible for physical deletion together with their corresponding SQLite index rows.
        • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-STARTUP-CLEANUP
          6.10. Asynchronous Expired Clipboard Cleanup GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-STARTUP-CLEANUP Expired Clipboard memory cleanup shall run asynchronously during MCP/server startup.

          Startup cleanup shall use authoritative expiration metadata and shall remove expired durable Clipboard files and corresponding index records coherently.
    • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ROOT
      7.1. Collection Memory Scope GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ROOT Collection Memory shall provide a persistent topic-oriented container into which explicitly requested memory episodes can be appended over time.

      A Collection is not an automatically recorded conversation.

      A Collection groups intentionally saved episodes around a user-defined subject or purpose.
      • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INIT
        7.2. Collection Initialization GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INIT Creating a Collection shall require:

        - Collection Name; and
        - Collection Description or Purpose.

        Initialization shall create a stable Collection identity and shall record its creation time.

        The underlying stable file_id shall serve as the Collection ID.
        • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-IDENTITY
          7.3. Stable Collection Identity GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-IDENTITY Collection ID shall remain stable independently of later episode appends.

          A Collection may be targeted for an append by:

          - exact Collection ID; or
          - exact Collection Name where that name resolves safely within the authenticated owner's scope.
      • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-EXPLICIT-APPEND
        7.4. Collection Append Is Explicit GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-EXPLICIT-APPEND A Collection shall receive a new episode only when the user explicitly asks GHOST to save or add content to that Collection.

        Normal conversation turns shall not be appended automatically merely because a Collection exists.
        • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-EPISODE-METADATA
          7.5. Collection Episode Description GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-EPISODE-METADATA Every appended Collection episode shall contain an Episode Description describing that episode's local contribution to the Collection.

          A Recall Key may be explicitly supplied or generated according to the shared Save policy.
        • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ACTIVEBRIEF
          7.6. Collection Cumulative ActiveBrief GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ACTIVEBRIEF Every appended Collection episode shall also carry the current cumulative Collection ActiveBrief.

          The Collection ActiveBrief shall summarize the accumulated knowledge or state of the Collection's fixed topic after incorporating the new episode.

          The Collection ActiveBrief is not a conversation-summary mechanism and shall not be confused with ActiveBlackboard merely because both use an ActiveBrief concept.
      • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-LIST
        7.7. List Collections GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-LIST GHOST shall support listing Collections for the authenticated owner.

        The Collection list shall provide sufficient metadata for deterministic identification, including at least:

        - Collection ID;
        - Collection Name;
        - Collection Description or Purpose; and
        - creation date.
        • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-LIST-EPISODES
          7.8. List Episodes in a Collection GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-LIST-EPISODES Given an exact Collection ID, GHOST shall support listing the episodes belonging to that Collection.

          The episode list shall return metadata for all Collection episodes, including:

          - Recall Key where present; and
          - Episode Description.

          This operation is metadata navigation and shall not automatically return the complete stored content of every episode.
      • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INDIVIDUAL-RECALL
        7.9. Individual Collection Episode Recall GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INDIVIDUAL-RECALL An individual Collection episode shall not require a separate Collection-specific recall mechanism when it has an exact Recall Key or Record ID.

        The shared exact Recall capability shall be used for an individual episode.
      • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-RECALL
        7.10. Collection Episode Range Recall GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-RECALL GHOST shall support Collection-specific retrieval by episode number or episode range.

        Examples include:

        - one episode such as episode 3; or
        - a range such as episodes 2 through 7.

        Episode ordering shall be deterministic within the Collection.
        • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-TOKEN-SAFETY
          7.11. Token-Safe Collection Range Recall GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-TOKEN-SAFETY When a requested Collection range would produce more content than can be returned safely in the active client/model context, GHOST may return a deterministic prefix of the requested range.

          The response shall explicitly identify the unreturned remainder so that the client can request it subsequently.

          The exact token threshold or page size is intentionally not fixed by this requirement.
      • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-WHOLE
        7.12. Whole Collection Delete GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-WHOLE Deleting an entire Collection shall be a separate destructive operation from deleting an individual memory episode.

        Whole-Collection deletion shall require the exact Collection ID.

        A Collection shall not be destroyed by semantic description, Collection Name similarity, or LLM selection.
        • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-CONFIRMATION
          7.13. Two-Step Whole Collection Delete Safety GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-CONFIRMATION Whole-Collection deletion shall use a temporary server-side confirmation state.

          For an authenticated owner and exact Collection ID, the first exact whole-Collection delete request shall not execute the deletion.

          The first request shall set the corresponding server-side delete-pending state to true and shall return a warning or refusal asking the client/user to repeat the same exact Collection deletion request.

          If the same owner repeats the exact whole-Collection delete request for the same Collection ID while that delete-pending state is true, GHOST shall execute the deletion and confirm the result.

          The delete-pending state shall be volatile server state and shall reset to false when the MCP server restarts.

          A future timeout or asynchronous reset policy may be added later, but no timeout duration or additional reset mechanism is fixed by this requirement.
      • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INDIVIDUAL-DELETE
        7.14. Individual Collection Episode Delete GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INDIVIDUAL-DELETE Deleting an individual episode from a Collection shall use the shared deterministic memory Delete behavior.

        No separate Collection-specific single-episode deletion contract is required.

    GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-OWNER-SCOPE
    3.3. Owner-Scoped Memory GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-OWNER-SCOPE Every persistent MCP memory operation shall be scoped to the authenticated owner.

    An exact key, record ID, Collection ID, Collection Name, Clipboard slot, or other selector shall never bypass owner isolation.

    GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE
    4.1.1. Shared Save Concept GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE GHOST shall expose one clear Save concept for ordinary memory episodes.

    The current executable tool identifier ghost_memory_tag represents the existing implementation of this save concept.

    A future rename of that tool is not approved by this requirement and shall require a separate interface-contract decision.
    • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-VISIBLE-CONTENT
      4.1.2. Save Visible Conversation Content GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-VISIBLE-CONTENT When saving a visible conversation episode, the selected visible user content and corresponding visible assistant content shall be stored without substitution by hidden reasoning, internal tool traffic, or an internal model/tool result.

      When exact visible content is required by the selected Save operation, ChatGPT shall pass that content without summarizing it.
    • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-TITLE-DESCRIPTION
      4.1.3. Episode Title and Description GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-TITLE-DESCRIPTION A newly saved ordinary memory episode shall have:

      - an Episode Title; and
      - an Episode Description.

      ChatGPT shall generate both from the selected visible episode unless a more specific mode requirement states otherwise.

      Episode Title is primarily human-facing metadata.

      Episode Description is the compact semantic description used by intelligent Episodic retrieval.
    • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-RECALL-KEY
      4.1.4. Recall Key Handling and Episodic Uniqueness GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-RECALL-KEY When the user explicitly provides a Recall Key, ChatGPT shall pass that key.

      When the user requests an Episodic save without providing a Recall Key, ChatGPT shall generate an appropriate Recall Key rather than forcing the user to invent one.

      Within an authenticated owner's Episodic Memory, the effective Recall Key shall be unique.

      Before saving a new Episodic episode, GHOST shall check the owner-scoped Episodic Recall Keys recorded in the SQLite/index layer.

      If the requested or generated base key is already used by an Episodic episode, GHOST shall deterministically allocate the next available numeric suffix using the form:

      base_key_1
      base_key_2
      base_key_3

      and so on.

      The originally supplied key shall remain the base key; GHOST shall not overwrite the existing episode.

      The successful save result shall return the actual effective Recall Key that was stored.

    GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-RECALL
    4.2.1. Shared Recall Concept GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-RECALL GHOST shall expose one Recall concept capable of selecting the appropriate retrieval path from the user's request.

    For Episodic Memory, Recall shall support:

    - deterministic exact retrieval when an exact Recall Key or exact Record ID is known; and
    - intelligent semantic retrieval when the user describes a memory without knowing its exact identifier.

    The two paths access the same Episodic Memory domain.
    • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-EXACT-RECALL
      4.2.2. Exact Recall GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-EXACT-RECALL An exact Recall Key or exact Record ID shall be handled deterministically.

      Exact identifiers shall directly select stored records within the authenticated owner's scope.

      Exact Recall shall not require semantic vector ranking.
    • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-NO-FAKE-EXACT-FILTER
      4.2.3. Exact Identifiers Are Not Intelligent-Retrieval Filters GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-NO-FAKE-EXACT-FILTER Recall Key and Record ID shall not be treated as approximate SQL narrowing filters for intelligent semantic retrieval.

      When an exact identifier is supplied, GHOST shall use the deterministic exact path.

      When the identifier is unknown, GHOST shall use the intelligent Episodic retrieval path defined in this document.

    GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-LIST
    4.3.1. Shared Memory List GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-LIST ghost_memory_list shall provide metadata discovery and navigation rather than full episode retrieval.

    The shared list capability shall be available for memory modes where listing is meaningful, except Clipboard Memory.

    The list capability may return identifying and descriptive metadata such as:

    - memory or conversation name;
    - memory type;
    - Recall Key;
    - Record ID;
    - Episode Title;
    - Episode Description; and
    - creation time.

    Stored full input/output bodies shall remain Recall content rather than List content.
    • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-LIST-FILTERS
      4.3.2. Deterministic List Filters GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-LIST-FILTERS The shared memory list operation shall support deterministic metadata filtering sufficient for practical discovery.

      Approved filter dimensions include:

      - memory or conversation name;
      - memory type;
      - date range; and
      - deterministic description matching.

      List shall not silently become semantic full-memory retrieval.

    GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE
    4.4.1. Deterministic Memory Delete GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE ghost_memory_delete shall delete individual memory episodes only through an exact selector:

    - exact Recall Key; or
    - exact Record ID.

    Delete shall never use semantic similarity, a natural-language description, Episode Description similarity, vector retrieval, fuzzy matching, or an LLM decision to choose what data to destroy.
    • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-DUPLICATE-SAFETY
      4.4.2. Duplicate Recall-Key Safety GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-DUPLICATE-SAFETY If an exact Recall Key resolves to multiple owner-scoped records, GHOST shall not silently choose an arbitrary record for deletion.

      The user shall be given deterministic identifiers sufficient to select the intended episode, or shall explicitly request deletion of all exact matches where that behavior is supported.
    • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-NO-CLIPBOARD
      4.4.3. Clipboard Excluded from Generic Delete GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-NO-CLIPBOARD Clipboard Memory shall not participate in the generic ghost_memory_delete operation.

      Clipboard lifecycle shall be controlled by its dedicated short-retention policy.

    GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-DUPLICATE-SAFETY
    4.4.2. Duplicate Recall-Key Safety GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-DUPLICATE-SAFETY If an exact Recall Key resolves to multiple owner-scoped records, GHOST shall not silently choose an arbitrary record for deletion.

    The user shall be given deterministic identifiers sufficient to select the intended episode, or shall explicitly request deletion of all exact matches where that behavior is supported.
    • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE
      4.4.1. Deterministic Memory Delete GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE ghost_memory_delete shall delete individual memory episodes only through an exact selector:

      - exact Recall Key; or
      - exact Record ID.

      Delete shall never use semantic similarity, a natural-language description, Episode Description similarity, vector retrieval, fuzzy matching, or an LLM decision to choose what data to destroy.
      • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-MODEL

    GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-NO-CLIPBOARD

    Clipboard lifecycle shall be controlled by its dedicated short-retention policy.

    GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-ROOT
    5.1. Episodic Memory Scope GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-ROOT Episodic Memory shall store ordinary persistent memory episodes that can later be recovered either:

    - directly through an exact Recall Key or Record ID; or
    - intelligently from a natural-language description.

    Direct Recall and intelligent retrieval shall be two access paths to the same Episodic Memory rather than separate memory types.
    • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DESCRIPTION-REQUIRED
      5.2. Episode Description Required for Episodic Save GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DESCRIPTION-REQUIRED Each newly saved Episodic Memory episode shall contain a non-empty Episode Description.

      The description shall summarize the semantic content or useful meaning of that individual episode sufficiently to support later intelligent retrieval.

      The Episode Description shall not be replaced by the Episode Title.
      • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DESCRIPTION-VECTOR
        5.3. Episode Description Embedding GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DESCRIPTION-VECTOR The Episode Description shall have a precomputed vector representation available for intelligent Episodic retrieval.

        The description embedding shall be created from the stored Episode Description rather than generated dynamically from the complete episode during every recall.
    • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-INTELLIGENT-QUERY
      5.4. Intelligent Recall Query Description GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-INTELLIGENT-QUERY When the user requests a memory without knowing an exact identifier, ChatGPT shall formulate the semantic description of the memory being sought.

      That query description shall be embedded at recall time and compared against stored Episode Description embeddings.
      • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DATE-NARROWING
        5.5. Optional Date Narrowing GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DATE-NARROWING Intelligent Episodic retrieval may first apply a deterministic SQL date-range filter when the user's request provides a relevant date or date interval.

        Date range is the approved deterministic narrowing dimension for the intelligent Episodic retrieval path.

        The intelligent path shall not invent key-prefix, title-prefix, or approximate Recall Key filtering as additional narrowing mechanisms.
      • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-COSINE-RANKING
        5.6. Episode Description Similarity Ranking GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-COSINE-RANKING After any optional date narrowing, intelligent Episodic retrieval shall compare the query-description vector with stored Episode Description vectors using cosine similarity or the equivalent cosine-ranking behavior of the selected vector implementation.

        Ranking shall be based primarily on Episode Description semantics.
        • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CANDIDATE-RETURN
          5.7. Compact Intelligent Recall Candidates GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CANDIDATE-RETURN The intelligent retrieval stage shall return only a small ranked candidate set to the client model.

          The target candidate set shall normally contain approximately five to ten candidates.

          Each candidate shall provide sufficient metadata for selection, including at least:

          - Record ID; and
          - Episode Description.

          The candidate stage shall not return the complete stored Q/A bodies for every candidate.
          • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CLIENT-SELECTION
            5.8. Client Model Candidate Selection GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CLIENT-SELECTION After receiving the compact ranked candidate descriptions, the invoking AI client may use the user's request and candidate descriptions to select the intended episode.

            The selection result shall resolve to an exact Record ID before the full episode is fetched.
            • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-EXACT-FINAL-FETCH
              5.9. Exact Final Episode Fetch GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-EXACT-FINAL-FETCH After intelligent candidate selection, GHOST shall fetch the chosen full episode deterministically by exact Record ID.

              Full episode content shall be loaded only after the candidate-selection step has resolved the exact stored record.
        • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-NO-TITLE-FIRST-FUNNEL
          5.10. No Mandatory Title-First Semantic Funnel GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-NO-TITLE-FIRST-FUNNEL Episode Title shall remain useful human-facing metadata but shall not be a mandatory first semantic-ranking stage before Episode Description similarity.

          The approved intelligent-retrieval path shall rank Episode Descriptions directly.

    - Episode Description.

    The candidate stage shall not return the complete stored Q/A bodies for every candidate.
    • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CLIENT-SELECTION
      5.8. Client Model Candidate Selection GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CLIENT-SELECTION After receiving the compact ranked candidate descriptions, the invoking AI client may use the user's request and candidate descriptions to select the intended episode.

      The selection result shall resolve to an exact Record ID before the full episode is fetched.
      • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-EXACT-FINAL-FETCH
        5.9. Exact Final Episode Fetch GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-EXACT-FINAL-FETCH After intelligent candidate selection, GHOST shall fetch the chosen full episode deterministically by exact Record ID.

        Full episode content shall be loaded only after the candidate-selection step has resolved the exact stored record.
    • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CANDIDATE-RETURN
      5.7. Compact Intelligent Recall Candidates GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CANDIDATE-RETURN The intelligent retrieval stage shall return only a small ranked candidate set to the client model.

      The target candidate set shall normally contain approximately five to ten candidates.

      Each candidate shall provide sufficient metadata for selection, including at least:

      - Record ID; and
      - Episode Description.

      The candidate stage shall not return the complete stored Q/A bodies for every candidate.
      • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-COSINE-RANKING
        5.6. Episode Description Similarity Ranking GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-COSINE-RANKING After any optional date narrowing, intelligent Episodic retrieval shall compare the query-description vector with stored Episode Description vectors using cosine similarity or the equivalent cosine-ranking behavior of the selected vector implementation.

        Ranking shall be based primarily on Episode Description semantics.
        • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-INTELLIGENT-QUERY
          5.4. Intelligent Recall Query Description GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-INTELLIGENT-QUERY When the user requests a memory without knowing an exact identifier, ChatGPT shall formulate the semantic description of the memory being sought.

          That query description shall be embedded at recall time and compared against stored Episode Description embeddings.
          • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-ROOT
            5.1. Episodic Memory Scope GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-ROOT Episodic Memory shall store ordinary persistent memory episodes that can later be recovered either:

            - directly through an exact Recall Key or Record ID; or
            - intelligently from a natural-language description.

            Direct Recall and intelligent retrieval shall be two access paths to the same Episodic Memory rather than separate memory types.
            • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-MODEL
              3.1. Four-Mode MCP Memory Model GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-MODEL The approved GHOST MCP memory model shall consist of four conceptual memory modes:

              1. Episodic Memory.
              2. Clipboard Memory.
              3. Collection Memory.
              4. ActiveBlackboard Memory.

              This document owns the first three modes.

              ActiveBlackboard is owned exclusively by 112_mcp_activeblackboard.sdoc.
              • GHOST-MCP-CAP-ROOT
                1.1. MCP Capability Scope GHOST-MCP-CAP-ROOT GHOST MCP shall support the approved Prompt Engineering capability and three non-ActiveBlackboard memory modes:

                - Episodic Memory;
                - Clipboard Memory; and
                - Collection Memory.

                ActiveBlackboard shall remain separately owned by 112_mcp_activeblackboard.sdoc.
                • GHOST-MCP-ROOT
                  1.1. GHOST MCP Capability Scope GHOST-MCP-ROOT GHOST shall provide a Model Context Protocol interface through which approved external AI clients can invoke explicitly exposed GHOST capabilities.

                  The MCP capability shall provide a controlled external boundary around approved GHOST functions without transferring ownership of those functions to the MCP transport layer.

                  MCP shall be represented as its own capability family in the GHOST requirement hierarchy.

    The approved intelligent-retrieval path shall rank Episode Descriptions directly.

    GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-ROOT
    6.1. Clipboard Memory Scope GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-ROOT Clipboard Memory shall provide short-lived, deterministic temporary memory slots for lightweight save-and-recall workflows.

    Clipboard Memory shall use the reserved slot identifiers:

    M1 through M100.
    • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RESERVED-KEYS
      6.2. Reserved Clipboard Routing GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RESERVED-KEYS M1 through M100 shall be reserved for Clipboard Memory.

      A normal Episodic save shall not silently store an M1-M100 key as an ordinary Episodic Recall Key.

      When a user explicitly requests saving to or recalling from M1-M100, the request shall be routed to Clipboard Memory behavior.
    • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-DAILY-FILE
      6.3. One Clipboard File Per Day GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-DAILY-FILE For each authenticated owner, Clipboard Memory shall use at most one Clipboard memory history file for a UTC day in which Clipboard content is saved.

      Clipboard storage shall not perform intra-day file rollover merely because several Clipboard episodes are appended.
    • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-APPEND-ONLY
      6.4. Append-Only Clipboard Storage GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-APPEND-ONLY Clipboard writes shall be append-only.

      Saving to an already used slot shall append a new episode with the same slot identifier rather than physically overwriting the older episode.

      For example, repeated saves to M7 may produce several historical M7 episodes in durable storage.
      • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-LATEST-RECALL
        6.5. Newest Matching Clipboard Recall GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-LATEST-RECALL Recall of a Clipboard slot shall return the newest owner-scoped episode with that exact slot identifier.

        Creation timestamps and deterministic ordering metadata shall be sufficient to identify the newest matching episode.
    • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-CONTENT
      6.6. Clipboard Episode Content GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-CONTENT A Clipboard episode shall store only the visible saved content and metadata required for deterministic slot storage and recall.

      Clipboard episodes shall not require or generate an Episode Description.

      Clipboard episodes shall not maintain an ActiveBrief.
    • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-NO-SEMANTIC-RETRIEVAL
      6.7. Clipboard Uses Exact Slot Recall Only GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-NO-SEMANTIC-RETRIEVAL Clipboard Memory shall not provide intelligent semantic retrieval.

      Clipboard Recall shall use the exact M1-M100 slot identifier and return the newest exact match.
    • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-NO-GENERIC-LIST-DELETE
      6.8. Clipboard Outside Generic List and Delete GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-NO-GENERIC-LIST-DELETE Clipboard Memory shall not participate in the shared generic memory List or Delete operations.

      The user-facing model shall treat Clipboard as a temporary slot mechanism rather than as a manually administered long-term memory archive.
    • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RETENTION
      6.9. Short Clipboard Retention GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RETENTION Clipboard Memory shall be short-lived.

      The approved default retention window shall be approximately ten days, represented through explicit expiration metadata rather than inferred from a filename.

      Expired Clipboard histories shall be eligible for physical deletion together with their corresponding SQLite index rows.
      • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-STARTUP-CLEANUP
        6.10. Asynchronous Expired Clipboard Cleanup GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-STARTUP-CLEANUP Expired Clipboard memory cleanup shall run asynchronously during MCP/server startup.

        Startup cleanup shall use authoritative expiration metadata and shall remove expired durable Clipboard files and corresponding index records coherently.

    GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RETENTION
    6.9. Short Clipboard Retention GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RETENTION Clipboard Memory shall be short-lived.

    The approved default retention window shall be approximately ten days, represented through explicit expiration metadata rather than inferred from a filename.

    Expired Clipboard histories shall be eligible for physical deletion together with their corresponding SQLite index rows.
    • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-STARTUP-CLEANUP
      6.10. Asynchronous Expired Clipboard Cleanup GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-STARTUP-CLEANUP Expired Clipboard memory cleanup shall run asynchronously during MCP/server startup.

      Startup cleanup shall use authoritative expiration metadata and shall remove expired durable Clipboard files and corresponding index records coherently.
