    GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ROOT
    7.1. Collection Memory Scope GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ROOT Collection Memory shall provide a persistent topic-oriented container into which explicitly requested memory episodes can be appended over time.

    A Collection is not an automatically recorded conversation.

    A Collection groups intentionally saved episodes around a user-defined subject or purpose.
    • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INIT
      7.2. Collection Initialization GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INIT Creating a Collection shall require:

      - Collection Name; and
      - Collection Description or Purpose.

      Initialization shall create a stable Collection identity and shall record its creation time.

      The underlying stable file_id shall serve as the Collection ID.
      • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-IDENTITY
        7.3. Stable Collection Identity GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-IDENTITY Collection ID shall remain stable independently of later episode appends.

        A Collection may be targeted for an append by:

        - exact Collection ID; or
        - exact Collection Name where that name resolves safely within the authenticated owner's scope.
    • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-EXPLICIT-APPEND
      7.4. Collection Append Is Explicit GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-EXPLICIT-APPEND A Collection shall receive a new episode only when the user explicitly asks GHOST to save or add content to that Collection.

      Normal conversation turns shall not be appended automatically merely because a Collection exists.
      • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-EPISODE-METADATA
        7.5. Collection Episode Description GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-EPISODE-METADATA Every appended Collection episode shall contain an Episode Description describing that episode's local contribution to the Collection.

        A Recall Key may be explicitly supplied or generated according to the shared Save policy.
      • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ACTIVEBRIEF
        7.6. Collection Cumulative ActiveBrief GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ACTIVEBRIEF Every appended Collection episode shall also carry the current cumulative Collection ActiveBrief.

        The Collection ActiveBrief shall summarize the accumulated knowledge or state of the Collection's fixed topic after incorporating the new episode.

        The Collection ActiveBrief is not a conversation-summary mechanism and shall not be confused with ActiveBlackboard merely because both use an ActiveBrief concept.
    • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-LIST
      7.7. List Collections GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-LIST GHOST shall support listing Collections for the authenticated owner.

      The Collection list shall provide sufficient metadata for deterministic identification, including at least:

      - Collection ID;
      - Collection Name;
      - Collection Description or Purpose; and
      - creation date.
      • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-LIST-EPISODES
        7.8. List Episodes in a Collection GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-LIST-EPISODES Given an exact Collection ID, GHOST shall support listing the episodes belonging to that Collection.

        The episode list shall return metadata for all Collection episodes, including:

        - Recall Key where present; and
        - Episode Description.

        This operation is metadata navigation and shall not automatically return the complete stored content of every episode.
    • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INDIVIDUAL-RECALL
      7.9. Individual Collection Episode Recall GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INDIVIDUAL-RECALL An individual Collection episode shall not require a separate Collection-specific recall mechanism when it has an exact Recall Key or Record ID.

      The shared exact Recall capability shall be used for an individual episode.
    • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-RECALL
      7.10. Collection Episode Range Recall GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-RECALL GHOST shall support Collection-specific retrieval by episode number or episode range.

      Examples include:

      - one episode such as episode 3; or
      - a range such as episodes 2 through 7.

      Episode ordering shall be deterministic within the Collection.
      • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-TOKEN-SAFETY
        7.11. Token-Safe Collection Range Recall GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-TOKEN-SAFETY When a requested Collection range would produce more content than can be returned safely in the active client/model context, GHOST may return a deterministic prefix of the requested range.

        The response shall explicitly identify the unreturned remainder so that the client can request it subsequently.

        The exact token threshold or page size is intentionally not fixed by this requirement.
    • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-WHOLE
      7.12. Whole Collection Delete GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-WHOLE Deleting an entire Collection shall be a separate destructive operation from deleting an individual memory episode.

      Whole-Collection deletion shall require the exact Collection ID.

      A Collection shall not be destroyed by semantic description, Collection Name similarity, or LLM selection.
      • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-CONFIRMATION
        7.13. Two-Step Whole Collection Delete Safety GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-CONFIRMATION Whole-Collection deletion shall use a temporary server-side confirmation state.

        For an authenticated owner and exact Collection ID, the first exact whole-Collection delete request shall not execute the deletion.

        The first request shall set the corresponding server-side delete-pending state to true and shall return a warning or refusal asking the client/user to repeat the same exact Collection deletion request.

        If the same owner repeats the exact whole-Collection delete request for the same Collection ID while that delete-pending state is true, GHOST shall execute the deletion and confirm the result.

        The delete-pending state shall be volatile server state and shall reset to false when the MCP server restarts.

        A future timeout or asynchronous reset policy may be added later, but no timeout duration or additional reset mechanism is fixed by this requirement.
    • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INDIVIDUAL-DELETE
      7.14. Individual Collection Episode Delete GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INDIVIDUAL-DELETE Deleting an individual episode from a Collection shall use the shared deterministic memory Delete behavior.

      No separate Collection-specific single-episode deletion contract is required.

    GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ACTIVEBRIEF
    7.6. Collection Cumulative ActiveBrief GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ACTIVEBRIEF Every appended Collection episode shall also carry the current cumulative Collection ActiveBrief.

    The Collection ActiveBrief shall summarize the accumulated knowledge or state of the Collection's fixed topic after incorporating the new episode.

    The Collection ActiveBrief is not a conversation-summary mechanism and shall not be confused with ActiveBlackboard merely because both use an ActiveBrief concept.

    7.7. List Collections GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-LIST GHOST shall support listing Collections for the authenticated owner.

    The Collection list shall provide sufficient metadata for deterministic identification, including at least:

    - Collection ID;
    - Collection Name;
    - Collection Description or Purpose; and
    - creation date.

    GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-RECALL
    7.10. Collection Episode Range Recall GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-RECALL GHOST shall support Collection-specific retrieval by episode number or episode range.

    Examples include:

    - one episode such as episode 3; or
    - a range such as episodes 2 through 7.

    Episode ordering shall be deterministic within the Collection.
    • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-TOKEN-SAFETY
      7.11. Token-Safe Collection Range Recall GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-TOKEN-SAFETY When a requested Collection range would produce more content than can be returned safely in the active client/model context, GHOST may return a deterministic prefix of the requested range.

      The response shall explicitly identify the unreturned remainder so that the client can request it subsequently.

      The exact token threshold or page size is intentionally not fixed by this requirement.

    GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-WHOLE
    7.12. Whole Collection Delete GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-WHOLE Deleting an entire Collection shall be a separate destructive operation from deleting an individual memory episode.

    Whole-Collection deletion shall require the exact Collection ID.

    A Collection shall not be destroyed by semantic description, Collection Name similarity, or LLM selection.
    • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-CONFIRMATION
      7.13. Two-Step Whole Collection Delete Safety GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-CONFIRMATION Whole-Collection deletion shall use a temporary server-side confirmation state.

      For an authenticated owner and exact Collection ID, the first exact whole-Collection delete request shall not execute the deletion.

      The first request shall set the corresponding server-side delete-pending state to true and shall return a warning or refusal asking the client/user to repeat the same exact Collection deletion request.

      If the same owner repeats the exact whole-Collection delete request for the same Collection ID while that delete-pending state is true, GHOST shall execute the deletion and confirm the result.

      The delete-pending state shall be volatile server state and shall reset to false when the MCP server restarts.

      A future timeout or asynchronous reset policy may be added later, but no timeout duration or additional reset mechanism is fixed by this requirement.
